name: MITRE ATLAS™
purpose: The attacker’s playbook against AI systems and AI agents, kept current as attacks are observed.
what: ATLAS 2026.10 holds 16 tactics, 129 techniques and 92 sub-techniques, with 77 case studies. Many of its newest entries are about AI agents.
aliases: Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems

binds.line: Nobody is bound by it, and nothing is audited against it.

verifiedBy.line: A knowledge base built from real attacks and red team demonstrations. There is no certification.

sits.line: The adversary column, beside the AI column: the threats the AI frameworks answer.

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. The changelog for release 2026.10, of 28 October 2026, counts 16 tactics, 129 techniques, 92 sub-techniques, 44 mitigations and 77 case studies, and a count of the data file agrees. The site describes ATLAS as ‘a globally accessible, living knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques involving AI’.

Read on 14 November 2026: the data repository’s license file reads Copyright 2021-2026 MITRE, licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The site’s own terms page (atlas.mitre.org/terms) says the same, but it is drawn by script and answers a plain request with 404.

related.line: ATLAS follows ATT&CK’s shape: tactics, techniques and sub-techniques.
The AI RMF states the outcomes; ATLAS shows what goes wrong.
